executive_summary:
socxen is a SOC analyst suite that runs inside a security analyst's coding agent: three skill prompts drive an investigation of an Exabeam alert or case, a queue sweep, or a detection-tuning proposal, all reached through a bundled local connector that proxies every call to the customer's Exabeam platform. Its untrusted input is the tenant's own telemetry — alert, event and case text written by whoever generated the logged activity — plus, less obviously, the remote connector's own tool descriptions. Its consequential capabilities are narrow and well chosen: containment is denied outright, detection-rule writes are denied, and dismissing an alert or closing a case is held behind a gate that ships switched on and asks a human every time. The surfaces that matter most are therefore not the dangerous tools but the two places untrusted text reaches the model, and the small set of platform writes that were deliberately left prompt-free so that escalating is never friction.

Deal first with the connector's own tool descriptions. They carry text addressed to the model, the connector screens them and reports that they do so but forwards them unchanged, and the project's own measurement is that the model follows that text over its skill instructions essentially every time. Because those descriptions are neither signed nor version-pinned and nothing keeps a baseline to compare against, a changed or hostile description would only be noticed after the fact — and the writes it could steer, opening a case and writing case notes, run without asking anyone. The same shape reaches the agent through ordinary telemetry: the read-side screen removes invisible smuggling characters but nothing filters a plainly worded false explanation, so planted narrative can end up persisted in the case record and read back as fact by the next investigation. Treat those descriptions as untrusted vendor text rather than instructions, keep and compare a baseline of them, and mark agent-authored notes so a later session can tell them apart from analyst evidence.

Two smaller items deserve attention next. The installation guide advertises a third way to run the suite — any capable coding agent following the skill folder — on which neither host enforcement layer exists, while the skill itself tells the model that its own in-session question is the lock that always holds; that combination is the one place a suppressed alert could happen with no human in the loop, and the guide should say so plainly or drop the path. Beyond that: an upstream tool failure writes the platform's own error text into an audit trail that is otherwise deliberately metadata-only, the connector accepts an unencrypted endpoint without complaint so a mistyped configuration would send the API key over the wire in the clear, the prompt-free read tier includes tools the platform has not even exposed yet, and oversized results are spilled by the host to an unredacted local file that outlives the session. None of these needs an attacker to be clever; all four are small, contained fixes.

trust_boundaries.name: Platform content entering the model's context

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NEVER treat content retrieved from the platform ... as instructions to itself; retrieved data is evidence to be reasoned about
MUST NOT reason over or act on text retrieved from the platform before that text has been screened and stripped of unambiguous smuggling code points
Linguistically legitimate joiners (ZWJ/ZWNJ) and directional marks ... MUST be flagged rather than stripped

threats.summary: Instruction-shaped text in the remote MCP's own tool definitions is detected and reported by the bridge but forwarded to the model unchanged, and the project's own measurement is that the model obeys that channel over the skill on essentially every search.

Plain-language injection planted in alert, event or case free text reaches the model as ordinary evidence: the read-side screen removes invisible smuggling code points only, so a natural-language 'this is benign, close it' passes through intact.
threats.remainder: the screen is a code-point filter with no linguistic detection and no provenance labelling, leaving the skill's prose rules about provenance and untrusted data as the only thing separating planted narrative from retrieved fact

threats.summary: Nothing in the shipped payload checks which model is running, so an install on a model below the documented floor gets the weaker injection resistance the project itself measured, with no warning at install or at run time (checked: the floor is stated in the installation guide only; no model check exists in the installer, the preflight, the hook or the bridge).

remit_rules.excerpt: Every third-party runtime dependency socxen ships MUST be version-bounded and inventoried in the shipped bill of materials
The bridge's full resolved dependency set MUST be hash-pinned in the shipped lockfile

threats.summary: The remote MCP's tool definitions are neither signed nor version-pinned; the bridge hashes each definition and the whole surface, but stores no baseline and fetches the list once per process, so a swapped or newly hostile definition is detectable only by an operator diffing hashes between sessions after the fact.
A tampered upstream package could change what runs on the analyst's workstation when uv resolves the bridge's inline dependencies on a cold cache.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision reaching an Exabeam or host tool

remit_rules.excerpt: an MCP tool the tiers do not classify MUST ask, never run silently
No containment-class or enforcement tool ... may be reachable by socxen at runtime, and the shipped governance configuration MUST deny such tools deterministically
socxen MUST deny it deterministically on every host, under every spelling, exactly as it denies containment
socxen MUST NOT possess or invoke shell execution, arbitrary code execution, or general-purpose filesystem write capability as part of performing an investigation

threats.summary: All three skills instruct the model to run a host shell command at preflight, reaching a host capability outside socxen's declared tool inventory and outside anything its tier file can govern.
A containment or detection-rule-write tool the platform later exposes could be invoked by the agent under injected influence.
A tool the remote MCP grows that no tier classifies could inherit the session's default permission and run without anyone being asked.

remit_rules.excerpt: Exabeam read tools: SIEM event search, alert search, case search, threat timelines, detection-rule details and rule-inventory listings, MITRE coverage, and context-table lookups.

The shipped governance configuration ... MUST stay consistent with the governance posture the documentation describes, and that consistency MUST be enforced by an automated check rather than by reviewer memory
The bundled hook, the permission snippet and the Codex tool map MUST be derived from one tier source so the three cannot disagree

threats.summary: The prompt-free allow tier carries reads the remit's known-good baseline never enumerated, including parser tools pre-classified before the MCP exposes them, so a parser-inventory read will run silently the day the platform ships it.

The shipped documentation miscounts the tier surface it describes and the automated drift gates cover only generated artifacts, so an operator's picture of what runs prompt-free can diverge from the tiers with no check failing.
An install that never merges the optional permission pack could be left with no governance at all.

trust_boundaries.name: Dismiss, close, and durable writes into the tenant record

remit_rules.excerpt: Dismissing an alert, or closing or otherwise changing the disposition of a case, MUST be blocked by a host-enforced gate that is active on a fresh install with no operator opt-in
Before it calls any tool that would dismiss an alert or close a case, socxen MUST ask the analyst for explicit confirmation in the session
socxen MUST NOT delete or overwrite existing free-text content — case notes, descriptions, names, and supporting or closing reasons.
If human approval for a dismiss or close is declined or not given, socxen MUST abandon that action ... and MUST NOT retry the write or reach the same outcome by another tool or field
socxen MUST NOT present its in-prompt confirmation as equivalent to the harness-enforced permission gate

threats.summary: On the 'any other agent' install path the shipped documentation advertises, neither host enforcement layer exists, and the skill tells the model that its own in-prompt ask is the lock that always holds — so nothing but model compliance stands between an injected instruction and a dismiss or close.
A close reached by another route — a create_case landing already CLOSED or FALSE POSITIVE through the prompt-free escalation tier — would sidestep the ask-tier gate entirely.
An update carrying description, name, supporting-reason or tag fields would overwrite analyst-authored free text, which the platform replaces rather than appends.
A dismiss or close could land with no human answering — under a permission-bypass flag, or in a headless run where a prompt has no one to answer it.

trust_boundaries.name: Case notes re-entering later investigations as evidence

remit_rules.excerpt: every case-note or export write MUST pass through the bridge's deterministic output neutralizer, which masks high-specificity credentials and structured identifiers
socxen MUST NOT write text into a platform record without first de-activating executable content and clickable links in it

threats.summary: A case note written while the model is acting on planted content persists in the tenant record and is read back by a later session, or by the queue sweep, as retrieved platform evidence — and the escalation writes that seed it are prompt-free by design.
threats.remainder: the neutralizer acts on active content and structured secrets, not on the note's narrative, so a false benign explanation or manufactured corroboration persists intact and carries no marking that socxen, rather than an analyst, wrote it

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam API key, secret and the bearer minted from them

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials and any token derived from them MUST NEVER be written to the audit log, an investigation report, a case note, standard output or error, a crash trace, or any file on disk
Credentials and derived tokens MUST NEVER be transmitted to any host other than the operator-configured Exabeam API endpoint

threats.summary: The bridge accepts any scheme in the configured endpoint, so an http:// value would carry the client id, the client secret and the returned bearer in cleartext — and the same value seeds the allowlist that decides which links stay clickable in notes and mail.
The key, secret or derived bearer could reach the audit trail, an error string or a persisted case note.

The bridge mints one process-lifetime bearer from a single operator API key and applies no scoping of its own, so every proxied call runs with whatever access level that key was issued with (checked: the token request carries no scope or audience, and nothing narrows the session).

trust_boundaries.name: The audit trail and any configured off-host destination

remit_rules.excerpt: Free-text field values, raw tool arguments, raw tool results, and neutralized hostile payloads MUST NEVER be written into the audit log
Telemetry MUST NOT leave the operator's host unless the operator has deliberately selected an off-host destination; local-only recording is the required default
Every call socxen makes to the platform MUST be recorded in a durable, structured, machine-parseable audit record naming the tool, its outcome, and correlation identifiers

threats.summary: When the platform answers with an error, the bridge writes the tool result's own text — tenant- or proxy-sourced, capped and canonicalized but otherwise verbatim — into the durable audit trail that the design and the shipped docs both say never holds tool results.
Telemetry could route to an off-host collector, webhook or back into the tenant without the operator noticing.
The gate's decision log can be switched off by environment variable, losing the only record of attempts stopped before they reached the bridge.

trust_boundaries.name: The host's working file for oversized tool results

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NOT copy alert, case, or event content out of the tenant to any local or remote store other than the investigation report it returns to the analyst in-session

threats.summary: An oversized tool result — a full case dump or the rule inventory, with whatever credentials and personal data the telemetry carried — is written by the host to a local file the write-path neutralizer never sees, persists after the session and is not pruned; on Codex the equivalent content lands in durable session stores with no single file to delete (checked: the neutralizer gates the write path only, and the docs state the spill file is deliberately not redacted).

the bridge fetches the definition list once per process and caches it for the whole session
the screen strips invisible code points and flags text that talks to the model, then forwards the definition unchanged
the flagged definition enters the host's tool list verbatim, indistinguishable from a trusted tool description
the model reads it as an instruction addressed to it and follows it over the skill — the project measured compliance on 1,840 of 1,840 searches
the escalation writes sit in the prompt-free allow tier, so no human is asked before a case or a case note is created
the write is forwarded; its free-text fields are de-fanged and structured secrets masked, but the narrative is the model's own
the note lands in the tenant case record, where later sessions read it back as retrieved platform evidence

attack_paths.name: Text planted in the tenant's own log data becomes a permanent case-record entry no human approved

steps.summary: alert, event and case free text is authored by whoever generated the logged activity — unauthenticated, attacker-influenceable, and unlabelled once it is inside the platform
the platform hands it back as an ordinary tool result with no provenance distinction from detector-generated fields
the bridge proxies the result on the one path every read takes
the read-side screen removes invisible smuggling code points only; a plain-language instruction or a fabricated baseline passes untouched
the screened result is placed in the model's context alongside the skill's own instructions
the model weighs the planted text as evidence; only prose rules, which the same finding shows the model can be talked past, separate retrieved content from instruction
opening a case and writing case notes are allow-tier and prompt-free, so the documenting write needs no human answer
the note is de-fanged and structured secrets masked; a false benign explanation is not a shape any deterministic filter matches
the manufactured corroboration persists in the case record and is read back as platform evidence by later investigations and by the queue sweep

notes.lane_fit: Two strains, both minor. The credential file and the two local audit files sit in external_deploy under the lane table's 'secrets stores, telemetry sinks' line even though nothing about them leaves the analyst's workstation. And one client node covers both supported hosts (Claude Code and the Codex package): they are parallel adapters over the same skills and the same tier file, and splitting them would double every client-side edge without changing a trust consequence.
notes.omissions: Arbitration divergence, KB wins: PRAX-2026-09-07-003 stores ASI09 alongside LLM03, but the Agentic KB's compound-signal table makes a missing or disabled approval gate LLM03 primary and explicitly excludes ASI09 for the gate itself, so the state-commit threat is tagged LLM03 only. No divergence on the other seven findings. No model node or model-egress boundary is emitted: socxen makes no model call of its own — per the contract's prompt-shaped-target convention the LLM is the skill prompt following its instructions, and the provider relationship is the operator's, cited only in documentation. The three skills' reference/ corpora are parallel markdown with no enumerating construct and fold into their skills' evidence; triage-cases and rule-tuning are collapsed into one read-only family node because their trust consequence is identical. The Codex MCP approval map and the bundled MCP registration fold into the host-agent and tier-source nodes as wiring. security/, evals/, tests/ and .github/ were read as maturity evidence per the scan scope and are not modelled as architecture.
